The defendant was inducted as a tenant by the plaintiff in respect of the basement and ground floor (area measuring approximately 4200 sq. ft.) at I2150, DSIDC, Narela, New Delhi on a monthly rent of CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. sentences.text: The tenancy was for a period of 11 months w.e.f. 01.01.2006.
The rent was duly paid against receipt till October 2006.
The tenanted premises was used as a ware house by the defendant to store its goods.
Defendant had agreed to pay electricity charges as per actual consumption @ Rs. 5.20 per unit.

The defendant had agreed and undertook to keep the tenanted premises in good condition, not to cause or let the premises suffer any damage thereto and deliver back vacant premises to plaintiff on termination of tenancy period in the same condition in which it was let out.

The tenancy premises were handed over by plaintiff to defendant in excellent condition as it was newly constructed having "A" grade building construction and electrical fittings having separate circuit and MCV's.
Earlier, the defendant was also the tenant in the basement of said premises for 11 months from December 2004 to October 2005 and had no complaints.
The building was also having fire extinguishers at all the floors.
At around 1.30 a.m. on the intervening night of 28/29.10.2006, a fire broke out in the tenancy premises.
Neighbours called fire brigade.
Plaintiff was informed by the Agent/Manager of the defendant at 9.00 a.m. on 29.10.2006.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The defendant was inducted as a tenant by the plaintiff in respect of the basement and ground floor (area measuring approximately 4200 sq. ft.) at I2150, DSIDC, Narela, New Delhi on a monthly rent of CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. Rs.32,000/ payable on or before 8th of every month by cheque by defendant.
Plaintiff CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs.
The fire broke in the tenanted portion due to negligence of defendant and had caused extensive damages to the said premises consisting of basement, ground floor and vacant first floor.
Plaintiff asked the Manager/Agent of the defendant for payment of the damages caused to the building by the fire, who stated that he would assess the amount of damages caused to the building by the fire and send the assessment and amount required for restoration/repair of the premises to his head office assuring the proposal would be sanctioned as assessed/proposed by him or premises would be restored to its original position by the defendant itself.
Since, neither defendant restored the tenanted premises to original condition nor paid the aforesaid demanded sum of Rs. 12,25,725/ nor paid the arrears of rent from November 2006 to December 2006, present suit was filed by CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs.
Mills India Pvt. Ltd.
3. In the written statement filed by defendant preliminary objections were taken as (i) the suit is misconceived and baseless; (ii) the tenanted premises were taken by defendant for purpose of using it as warehouse for storage of food items sold by defendant and while entering into lease, plaintiff assured defendant that the said property was free from CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs.
General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. all defects and the wiring installed in the said property was the best and defendant would not have any problem with regard to the usage of said property but no fire safety equipments were installed therein nor ever installed during tenancy period; (iii) at no point of time any combustible or hazardous goods were stored in the tenanted premises by the defendant;
(iv) the defendant after taking the premises on rent did not carry out any changes either in the structure or in the electrical fittings installed in the tenanted premises; (v) when the fire broke out on the fateful night, neither any representative of defendant was present at the warehouse nor the warehouse was open nor any combustible or hazardous goods were stored in the warehouse.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It stands not proved that PW 2 was any expert.
It is the case of defendant that its representatives were not permitted to enter into the premises after the lock was put over tenanted premises by plaintiff and even their request for letting them get the premises inspected from an Architect went without favour with plaintiff.
So,
defendant was unable to get the premises inspected to go at the root cause of fire.
It is the case of the plaintiff, as per replication, that tenanted premises were left deserted, abandoned and open by defendant and when informed by neighbours on 28.12.2006, plaintiff found nothing in the premises, which was badly damaged and even the electrical and sanitary fittings were removed.

Since plaintiff has not filed alleged completion certificate of the suit property and sanction plan of the suit property alongwith the plaint or even later with permission of the court, there is no option with CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. the court to presume the existence of fact as per illustration (g) of Section 114 of Indian Evidence Act, 1872 that the documentary evidence which could be produced by plaintiff and has not been produced by him, so if was produced by him, would have been unfavourable to him having been with held.
Necessary ) C.S. No.87/2007 vs General Mills India Pvt. Ltd on 30 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108381548/
8 inference is that either plaintiff had not taken any steps for getting any plan sanctioned nor obtained any completion certificate with respect to the suit property or had constructed the suit property unauthorizedly in violation of the building bylaws and regulations in vogue.
Be that as it may, fact remains that despite it being own case of plaintiff that his property suffered damages on account of fire allegedly caused due to the negligent act of defendant, neither plaintiff has filed any document for installation of fire extinguishers in the suit property or refilling them or having obtained any fire safety certificate or having renewed any fire safety certificate from authorities.
Even, plaintiff has not placed on record any document with respect of construction raised in the tenanted premises,
electrical wiring installed there to prove, even by preponderance of probabilities, that he (plaintiff)
had used standard and quality equipments in such construction and installation of electric wirings confirming ISI or BIS standards, as the CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs.
. PW1 claimed that fire had taken place due to short circuit in the office of defendant.
It is a mere bald assertion of PW1 for which no oral or documentary cogent evidence has been led in support thereof in corroboration.
No Structural Certificate of tenanted premises has been obtained nor filed nor proved.
No report of any Electrical Engineer has been filed nor proved to prove relevant fact that it was negligent act of defendant due to which fire took place.
There is no cogent evidence on record that there was any combustible or hazardous material in the warehouse/tenanted premises of defendant which led to breaking of fire.
PW1 denied of taking place of fire due to short circuiting because of his installed wiring material of sub standard quality but PW1 CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. himself did not place on record nor proved any document with respect to the wiring material installed in the tenanted premises in question to be of standard quality. PW1 claims of being informed on 28.12.2006 by neighbours that defendant had deserted, abandoned and left open the suit property.
At the time of filing of the suit, possession of the tenanted suit property was with the plaintiff.
Plaintiff has failed to prove when he regained the possession of tenanted suit premises from defendant/otherwise by any cogent, admissible, oral or documentary evidence by preponderance of probabilities, to claim rent or charges for use and occupation of tenanted suit premises post fire by defendant.
For the claim laid in counter claim of defendant there is no admissible cogent evidence on record.
